question:
Consider $f(x)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^2+1}\right)$.

(i) Determine its domain and range.

(ii) Verify whether its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.

(iii) Find its greatest value and the point at which it is attained. Do not draw the graph.

options.A: Domain: $\mathbb{R}$; Range: $\left[0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right]$; the function is even; greatest-value point: $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
options.B: Domain: $\mathbb{R}$; Range: $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right]$; the function is odd; greatest-value point: $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
options.C: Domain: $\mathbb{R}$; Range: $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right]$; the function is even; greatest-value point: $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
options.D: Domain: $\mathbb{R}-\{0\}$; Range: $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$; the function is even; greatest value is not attained
